newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Consortia in Brazil CVRD bid unsettled.
newsitem.headline: Consortia in Brazil CVRD bid unsettled.

text.p: Two consortia emerging as likely bidders in the privatization of Brazil's state mining giant CVRD could face stumbling blocks in their efforts to build a group of interested investors.

A third consortium is in the making and it is widely assumed there will be at least two if not three consortia bidding on April 29, when the government sells off a 45 percent block of CVRD voting shares for a base price of three billion reais ($2.83 billion).

Brazil's largest steelmaker Companhia Siderurgica Nacional (CSN) could find itself back to square one in its efforts to scramble together a consortium, after its main partners Bradesco and South Africa's Gencor Ltd look to be out of the race.

The other consortium forming around Brazilian metal, cement and pulp group Votorantim could face problems if moves by lower house deputies to discredit South Africa's Anglo American Corp of South Africa as a potential bidder bore fruit.
"We believe there will be at least two consortia," said Tereza Cristina Aquino, the BNDES superintendant for the privatization of CVRD. "It looks like a third one is in the process of being formed."

Bradesco, Brazil's largest retail bank, is not allowed to participate in any consortium bidding for CVRD, given that it was a member of the consultative group which evaluated CVRD for privatization, but it says it will lend support to the CSN bid.

Gencor has issued a statement in South Africa, saying it will not pursue a bid for CVRD because "a leading role in the management of CVRD...would not contribute sufficiently to Gencor's global strategy".
However, CSN has shrugged off the statement, saying all it meant was that Gencor did not seek a leading position within the consortium.

"CSN's understanding is that Gencor is not pursuing a leading position within the consortium, which is exactly what the company wants," a CSN spokesman said. "We want the consortium to be based on a model of shared control."
Aquino said CSN would probably persist in its efforts to find other bidding partners if Gencor really dropped out.
"It is possible that CSN will join other companies or a third consortium that is emerging," Aquino said. "CSN has had very firm intentions from the beginning to participate in the privatization."

Meanwhile, in the lower house of Congress, a group of deputies is on the warpath against the CVRD privatization and is trying to stall the process by prompting an inquiry into Anglo American's ties to investment bank Merrill Lynch and Co Inc, a consultant in the CVRD privatization.
They allege Merrill Lynch's ownership of a South African brokerage which acts as a sponsoring broker for Anglo American represents a conflict of interest. Merrill Lynch has rejected the accusation.
The third consortium could consist of Australian mining firm WMC Ltd, Japan's Mitsui Co Ltd, Brazil's iron ore miner MBR and possibly Anglo-Australian mining conglomerate RTZ-CRA.
